_comment: Declarative disk-full defense. Source of truth for: per-mount watch thresholds, systemd-tmpfiles cleanup rules, journald limits, docker retention, and reclaim actions. Nix module `configuration_system-protection.nix` reads this file and generates systemd units + tmpfiles.d + logrotate rules. Change what gets protected = edit this file, `build.sh ship` home-manager.

emergency._comment: HARD stop-the-bleeding tier, ABOVE every per-mount critical. RECLAIM-FIRST ORDER (2026-07-08 incident fix): the 2026-07-08 freeze was this tier firing every 5min, each time SIGTERM+FREEZING workload.slice BEFORE reclaim — but reclaim (docker prune of ~23GB dangling layers) would have freed the space with ZERO disruption. New order runs ALL reclaim first, then `recheck_gate` re-reads usage: if reclaim self-healed the mount (< pct), the freeze/kill/thaw are SKIPPED entirely — the box is never disrupted. Only if reclaim was insufficient does the last-resort freeze (pause writes, reversible) + kill (SIGTERM) run. `cooldown_minutes` prevents re-SIGTERM'ing the same slices every 5min when the disk is genuinely full of non-reclaimable data (that repeated kill was the spawn-storm that killed the session). `protected_slices` (os-essentials = ssh/wg/session/watchdog; connectivity = the untouchable island hosting freeze-guard) is NEVER killed or frozen. Defaults target workload.slice (background docker/nix-daemon), never the live desktop (user-1000.slice). recheck_gate MUST sit AFTER all reclaim and BEFORE freeze/kill; thaw MUST stay last (it always runs, defensively un-freezing even if a prior run stranded a slice).

watches._comment: Per-mount threshold-triggered actions. `critical_pct` fires the action list. Actions defined in `actions` map below.

mounts.description: tmpfs root — NixOS impermanence; filling blocks login, breaks systemd

btrfs user data — slow-fill; primary dev workspace. MUST be /home/diego, not /home: /home itself is NOT a mountpoint (the subvolumes are @home-diego and @home-guest, mounted at /home/diego and /home/guest), so the watchdog's `mountpoint -q` guard silently skipped it and this volume was never checked once.
btrfs guest home — same subvolume family as /home/diego.

tmpfs, size=2G. UNLIKE every btrfs entry here this has a REAL independent limit, and it is backed by RAM: filling it consumes 2G of an 8G machine, so a disk-fill here surfaces as an OOM kill rather than ENOSPC. Thresholds are deliberately tighter than the btrfs volumes because there is no reclaim path — nothing to GC, nothing to prune, the only fix is to stop the writer.
tmpfs, defaults to 50% of RAM. Same RAM-backed hazard as /tmpfs — a leaking shm segment is invisible to every btrfs check in this file.
btrfs @shared — persistent app state, audit logs, configs
Nix store — only shrinks via gc
p5 ext4 — Docker data-root + the dev-store chroot Nix store (~25G dev toolchain off the pool)

btrfs_qgroups._comment: WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS: the pool `/dev/mapper/pool` (~80G, ~64G used) hosts multiple btrfs subvolumes (@home-diego, @home-guest, @shared, @nixos/nix, @shared/tmp, @shared/journal) that ALL share one free-space pool. Without btrfs qgroups (quotas), `df` on every one of those mountpoints reports the SAME pool-wide used/avail numbers — there is no such thing as '/home/diego is at 95%' while the pool is at 60%, because df has no per-subvolume concept to report. The `watches.mounts` df-based checks above are therefore only ever measuring the WHOLE POOL's fill level once per subvolume that happens to live on it; a single subvolume silently ballooning (e.g. runaway ~/.cache, a leaked docker overlay, a git worktree explosion under /home/diego) is invisible until the pool itself is critical, by which point every subvolume on it is equally starved. Enabling btrfs qgroups makes per-subvolume accounting EXIST: each subvolume gets a 0/<subvolid> qgroup with its own `rfer` (referenced bytes) and, if `limit_gib` is set, a kernel-ENFORCED `max_rfer` cap that ENOSPCs writes to that subvolume specifically once it is hit — independent of how much free space the pool has left. That is what lets the watchdog answer 'is THIS subvolume overfull', which today is unrepresentable. WARNING — ACTIVATION COST: the FIRST `btrfs quota enable` on a filesystem that has never had quotas triggers a full one-time qgroup rescan (btrfs walks every extent to build initial accounting) — this is IO- and CPU-heavy and, on this ~64G-used pool, can take from a couple of minutes to tens of minutes depending on extent count/fragmentation, during which btrfs qgroup numbers are provisional (`btrfs qgroup show` shows a rescan-in-progress state) and filesystem IO latency is elevated. Do this at a time you can tolerate it, not mid-build. Every subsequent boot is a no-op (btrfs-qgroup-setup.sh checks `btrfs qgroup show` output first and only calls `quota enable` if it reports disabled). `limit_gib` is OPTIONAL per entry: leave it unset/null to get accounting + watchdog alerting with NO kernel-enforced cap (soft monitoring only); set it to also let the kernel itself refuse writes past that size regardless of what the watchdog does or how busy it is.

subvolumes.description: primary dev workspace — most likely to runaway (git worktrees, caches, containers under home)
guest home — hard-capped at 15G so a guest session can never starve diego's workspace or the pool
persistent app state/audit logs — includes @shared/tmp and @shared/journal as nested subvols, watched separately by their own mountpoints
nix store — only shrinks via gc, same threshold family as the existing df-based /nix watch

tmpfiles_rules._comment: Written to /etc/tmpfiles.d/50-cloud-data-disk-protection.conf via nix module. Format: `d <path> - - - <age> -`. Age in d (days), h (hours), m (minutes).
tmpfiles_rules._comment_dev-store: The last rule PROVISIONS (not cleans) a diego-owned DEV-STORE root on /mnt/shared-lib (p5, ~83G free) — a chroot Nix store (storeDir=/nix/store) holding the heavy dev toolchain (~25G) OFF the 80G pool. /mnt/shared-lib is root-owned ext4 so the user-tier home-manager cannot create it; the NixOS host does, here. Populated by bc_flakes_dev-store/build.sh, entered via the `dev` bwrap shell. Supersedes the 2026-06-18 android-only dirs — android-emulator is now a normal dev leaf inside this store. Plan: 0_tasks/PLAN_dev-store-split.md.

tmp_mounts._comment: Dedicated /tmp (btrfs, persistent, 3d age) + /tmpfs (RAM, ephemeral, 1d age). Decouples scratch from the 2G impermanence root so a leaky script can no longer block login by filling /. Nix module `configuration_tmp.nix` reads this and generates fileSystems.* + tmpfiles D! rules + activation-script that creates missing btrfs subvolumes. Rationale: previously /tmp lived inside tmpfs root and routinely hit 97% from orphaned working copies (e.g. /tmp/cloud-clean-work).

mounts.description: Large persistent scratch — wiped on boot, age 3 days. Use for build dirs, git worktrees, anything that might grow.
Fast RAM-backed scratch — 2G cap, wiped on every boot (tmpfs is RAM). Use for quick cache, ipc, workloads that benefit from RAM speed.

journald_limits._comment: systemd-journald.conf values — SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH, applied via configuration_system-protection-disk.nix `services.journald.extraConfig`. RATE-LIMITING (2026-07-08 incident fix): the freeze had ~87k journal lines/min from a systembus-notify restart loop + dead-unit polling, because rate-limiting was hardcoded OFF (RateLimitBurst=0) in configuration_persistence.nix. That log storm pegged the CPU and helped collapse the session. RateLimitBurst=10000 per RateLimitIntervalSec=30s caps any single service to ~20k lines/min (vs 87k) — a runaway unit can no longer flood journald/CPU. MaxLevelStore=info drops debug-spam from disk. persistence.nix now owns ONLY storage/sync/seal keys (no rate-limit, no levels) to avoid the previous two-writer collision.

journal_flood_guard._comment: The invisible-failure-mode voter (2026-07-08). That freeze had a ~87k-lines/min journald storm (systembus-notify restart loop + dead-unit polling) that NO PSI voter could see — memory/cpu/io PSI were ~0 at slice level throughout, so freeze-guard never fired. This guard watches the AGGREGATE journal line-rate over a 60s window: if it exceeds `lines_per_min_max`, it finds the single loudest unit and restarts it (breaking a restart/poll loop at the source) + urgent ntfy. Complements the per-unit journald RateLimitBurst cap: that bounds ONE unit's rate; this bounds the aggregate and acts on the offender. Runs isolated in os-essentials.slice (idle IO) — deliberately NOT inside freeze-guard's loop, so a bug here can never take down the PSI killer. `never_restart` protects units whose restart would be harmful or pointless.

docker_retention._comment: Weekly `docker system prune` guarded by free-space check. Only prunes when real disk is >75% full to avoid churning healthy state.

cargo_sweep._comment: cargo-sweep keeps ~/.cargo/target/ bounded. Runs weekly; keeps only targets touched in last `keep_days`.

nix_gc._comment: Nix store garbage collection. Keeps generations younger than `keep_days`.

script_hygiene._comment: CI lint rules for scripts that create tmp dirs. Each violation fails CI.

actions._comment: Action definitions. Nix module generates the corresponding ExecStart for disk-watchdog.service.

purge_tmp_worktrees.description: Remove orphaned worktree dirs under /tmp (no active process)

purge_audit_old.description: Delete /mnt/shared/log/audit/* older than 3 days (auditd rotation backstop)

docker_prune_builder.description: Prune the docker BUILD CACHE (buildkit layers) — `docker builder prune -af`. Build cache is NEVER referenced by a running container (docker system df reports it 0 active), so pruning it all is 100% safe. Root cause of the 2026-07-10 freeze: p5 filled to 97% with ~16GB of build cache from image rebuild loops (waydroid/caddy/superset), which docker_prune_images (dangling images only) and nix_gc (pool, not p5) could NOT touch — so RECLAIM was always INSUFFICIENT and the guard fell through to freezing workload.slice. This is the reclaim action that actually frees that space.

docker_prune_volumes_dangling.description: Prune dangling docker volumes — NEVER named volumes

dev_store_gc.description: GC the p5 dev-store chroot Nix store (keeps the current profile gcroot)

emergency_signal.description: VERBOSE journal (logger -t disk-emergency -p user.alert) + urgent ntfy + wall broadcast — explains which mount is full, the %, and exactly what the watchdog is about to do. The unmissable 'disk is full, writes are being stopped for cleanup' signal.

kill_nonsystem.description: SIGTERM every process in emergency.kill_slices (non-system background tier). Stops the bleeders writing. os-essentials.slice is never targeted.

freeze_nonsystem.description: cgroup-v2 freeze of emergency.freeze_slices — survivors' writes halt instantly (paused, reversible, no data loss) while reclaim runs.

thaw_nonsystem.description: Un-freeze emergency.freeze_slices. ALWAYS runs (ungated) and last, so a transient spike or a prior run interrupted between freeze and thaw never leaves a slice stranded frozen. Thawing an already-thawed slice is a harmless no-op.

recheck_gate.description: Re-read the mount usage AFTER all reclaim actions. If now < emergency.pct, the reclaim SELF-HEALED the disk: set the gate so freeze_nonsystem + kill_nonsystem are SKIPPED (the box is never disrupted), log + default-priority ntfy 'self-healed'. If still >= pct, reclaim was insufficient and the last-resort freeze/kill proceed. Position in the actions list is the contract: everything reclaim BEFORE it, freeze/kill AFTER it.

testers._comment: Each tester verifies one invariant of the disk defense. Wire into reports-logs or a dedicated CI job.

checks.description: disk-watchdog.service is active on all VMs + desktop
systemd-tmpfiles lists our worktree rule
journald SystemMaxUse matches config
Every container has max-size=10m
tmpfiles.clean is actually cleaning
/tmp is its own btrfs mount (not inside tmpfs root)
/tmpfs is its own tmpfs RAM mount
@shared/tmp btrfs subvolume exists on pool
systemd-tmpfiles has D! /tmp rule (wipe on boot)
systemd-tmpfiles has D! /tmpfs rule (age + wipe on boot)
Root tmpfs usage < 50% (since /tmp is no longer on it)
auditd writes to /mnt/shared (btrfs), not /var/log/audit on tmpfs
/mnt/shared/log/audit lives on btrfs
tmpfiles has e rule that ages /mnt/shared/log/audit at 3d
/ watch's critical action list includes purge_audit_old
emergency tier fires at 95%
os-essentials.slice (ssh/wg/session/watchdog) is NEVER killed or frozen
emergency action list starts with the signal and ends with the thaw (so a spike never leaves a slice frozen)
no protected slice is also a freeze/kill target (never freeze ssh/session)

RECLAIM-FIRST invariant: docker_prune_images comes before recheck_gate, which comes before freeze_nonsystem and kill_nonsystem — so reclaim always runs before any freeze/kill and can self-heal without disruption
thaw_nonsystem is the final action (ungated safety un-freeze)

2026-07-10 root cause: docker BUILD CACHE (not dangling images) filled p5, so reclaim must run `docker builder prune` BEFORE recheck_gate or the guard can never self-heal and freezes. Assert docker_prune_builder is in the emergency reclaim list, before the recheck gate.
The /mnt/shared-lib (p5, docker data-root) critical tier prunes build cache at 90% — 5 points before the 95% emergency tier can arm, so build-cache fill self-heals early without any freeze.
docker_prune_builder action exists, is safe_mode, and prunes the build cache
cooldown_minutes >= 1 so a full disk cannot re-SIGTERM the same slices every 5min (the spawn-storm)
connectivity.slice (freeze-guard's island) is explicitly protected, not safe-by-omission
journald rate-limiting is ON (RateLimitBurst > 0) — a runaway unit cannot flood journald/CPU as in the 2026-07-08 87k-lines/min storm
checks.command: systemctl show systemd-journald -p LogRateLimitBurst --value 2>/dev/null; grep -h '^RateLimitBurst=' /run/systemd/journald.conf.d/*.conf /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/*.conf /etc/systemd/journald.conf 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d= -f2

checks.description: no config sets RateLimitBurst=0 (unlimited) — the persistence.nix footgun is gone
the hardcoded /-only disk-watchdog (docker prune -af / nix-collect-garbage -d footgun) is removed; only disk-watchdog-v2 remains
journal-flood-guard timer is active — the PSI-blind log-storm voter is armed

deployment.deploy_to_vms_command: for vm in gcp-proxy gcp-t4 oci-mail oci-analytics oci-apps; do (cd ~/git/cloud/b_infra/nixhm-sudo-$vm && ./build.sh ship); done
